claims.statement: The auth domain is wired through svcs factories in `register_auth_services` (UserRepository, VerificationTokenRepository, TotpRepository, RecoveryCodeRepository, PasskeyRepository, EmailVerificationService, TotpService, PasskeyService, AuthorizationApi, UserApi), and `auth_router` is mounted under the `/api/v1` prefix while the WebSocket router is mounted separately at `/api/ws`.

Access tokens are HS256 JWTs signed with `settings.secret_key` carrying `sub` = email, `user_id`, `exp` (24 hours), `scope="access"`, and a random `jti`; they are minted by `UserApi.create_access_token`.

MFA tokens are HS256 JWTs with a 5-minute expiry, `scope="mfa_pending"` and no `jti`; `UserApi.verify_mfa_token` rejects any token whose scope is not `mfa_pending` with 401, so the scope assertion is bidirectional with the `access` check.

`UserApi.get_current_user_from_token` rejects expired tokens (401 `Token expired`), non-`access` scopes (401 `Token invalid`), denylisted `jti`s (401 `Token revoked`), and emails with no user record, returning a `User` only when every check passes.

`UserApi.revoke_token` writes `token:deny:{jti}` to Redis with `setex` for the token's remaining lifetime so the denylist cannot outlive the token, and silently ignores malformed or already-expired tokens.

The `get_token` dependency resolves the session from the `auth_token` cookie or an OAuth2 Bearer header and raises 401 `Not authenticated` when neither is present; `current_user` yields the `User` produced by `UserApi.get_current_user_from_token`.

`UserApi.login` returns 401 for unknown emails (after a dummy argon2 verify that equalizes timing) and for wrong passwords, raises the unverified-user branch as 403, and returns a 2FA challenge (`mfa_token`, no session) instead of an access token when a verified TOTP record exists.

The login route sets the `auth_token` cookie with `httponly` and `secure` only when `environment == "prod"`, `samesite="lax"` and a 7-day `max_age`, updates `last_login_at`, logs `auth.login_failure` with the attempted email on both failure branches and `auth.login_success` with the user id on success.

`POST /auth/2fa/login-verify` re-validates the `mfa_pending` token, requires an existing active user, verifies the code through `TotpService.verify_2fa_login`, then mints an access token, sets the same 7-day cookie, and updates `last_login_at`.

Email verification tokens are `itsdangerous` `URLSafeTimedSerializer` payloads `{email, nonce}` with salt `email-verification`, persisted with `expires_at` derived from `settings.email_verification_token_expiry_hours`; issuing a new token first marks every prior token for that user as used.

`verify_token` requires an existing, unused, unexpired token whose serializer payload email resolves to the same `user_id` as the stored row, then marks the user verified and the token used, making each verification link single-use.

`resend_verification` returns silently for unknown or already-verified emails to prevent enumeration, while SMTP failures surface as HTTP 502 from both the signup and resend-verification routes (signup's 502 states the account exists but the email failed).

`EmailService.send_email` renders Jinja HTML and text templates from `src/templates/email`, sends over `aiosmtplib` using the `smtp_*` settings, and raises `EmailSendError` on any failure; the verification link is `settings.frontend_url` + `/auth/verify-email?token=...`.

TOTP setup generates a `pyotp` base32 secret and a `Retail Portfolio` provisioning URI while leaving the record unverified; activation verifies the submitted code with `valid_window=1`, marks the record verified, and issues exactly 8 argon2-hashed recovery codes of the form `{token_hex(4)}-{token_hex(4)}` after deleting previous codes.

Login-time 2FA verification treats a 6-character all-digit code as TOTP and anything else as a recovery code, consuming a matching recovery code via `mark_as_used` (with `used_at`) so a code cannot be replayed.

2FA verification is throttled through the Redis key `2fa:lockout:{user_id}`: at or above `settings.totp_max_attempts` the request returns 429 before any code comparison, a failed attempt is `INCR`-ed and given `settings.totp_lockout_seconds` TTL, and a successful attempt deletes the key.

Passkey registration stores the challenge at `webauthn:challenge:reg:{user_id}` with `settings.webauthn_challenge_ttl_seconds` and consumes it atomically with `getdel`, verifying the attestation against `webauthn_rp_id`/`webauthn_origin` with `require_user_verification=False`; an expired or replayed challenge fails with 400.

Passkey authentication options are unauthenticated and store the challenge at `webauthn:challenge:auth:{challenge}`; verification resolves the passkey by credential id (401 when unknown), requires an active user (401) and a verified email (403), consumes the challenge with `getdel` (400 when expired), verifies the assertion, and persists the new `sign_count` and `last_used_at`.
Passkey sign-in is a first-class session path: `POST /auth/passkey/authenticate/verify` mints an access token, sets the same `auth_token` cookie as password login, and updates `last_login_at`.

`POST /api/v1/auth/ws-ticket` requires the `auth_token` cookie, validates it through `UserApi.get_current_user_from_token`, and returns an `itsdangerous`-signed JSON payload `{user_id, jti}` with salt `ws-ticket` signed by `settings.secret_key`.

The `/api/ws` handshake prefers the `ticket` query parameter, rejects replays via a Redis `SET NX EX 30` key on the ticket's SHA-256 hash, accepts tickets only within `max_age=30`, otherwise falls back to the `auth_token` cookie or `sec-websocket-protocol` token verified through `UserApi`, and closes with code 1008 on any failure.
The worker dashboard WebSocket reuses the same `ws-ticket` format and replay-protection helper, while its REST task routes are gated by `Depends(current_user)`.

`AuthorizationApi.check_entity_owned_by_user` raises 404 `Entity does not exist` when the entity is `None` or owned by another user, account/portfolio/integration routers call it instead of comparing ids, and `src/main.py` maps `AuthorizationError` to 404 so existence is never confirmed with 403.

The SvelteKit SSR guard verifies the `auth_token` cookie with `jose.jwtVerify` using `JWT_SECRET` and `algorithms: ['HS256']`, deletes the cookie for any non-`access` scope or verification failure (leaving `locals.user` null), redirects unauthenticated requests to `/auth/login`, redirects authenticated users away from `/auth/login` and `/auth/signup`, and honors `clear_session=true` to break stale-cookie redirect loops.

`frontend/src/lib/server/auth-cookie.ts` defines `AUTH_COOKIE_OPTS` (path `/`, `httpOnly`, `sameSite: 'lax'`, `secure` when not dev) and `deleteAuthCookie`; those attributes must match the `cookies.set('auth_token', ...)` calls in the login actions or browser deletes silently no-op.

The frontend login actions set the `auth_token` cookie (path `/`, `httpOnly`, `sameSite: 'lax'`, `secure` when not dev, 1-week `maxAge`) on single-factor, 2FA, and passkey success; they return `requires2fa`/`mfaToken` without a cookie when the backend answers with a challenge, and map a backend 403 to the "Email not verified" message.

Server loads that receive a 401 from the backend call `deleteAuthCookie` and redirect to `/auth/login?clear_session=true`, a pattern repeated on `/`, `/accounts/[id]`, `/brokers`, `/security/[security_id]`, and `/settings/security`.

The login form renders the 2FA challenge (6-digit code with a recovery-code toggle) when the action returns `requires2fa`, and offers passkey sign-in that fetches options, runs `startAuthentication`, and posts the serialized credential to the `passkeyLogin` action.

`/settings/security` loads 2FA status and passkeys in parallel and drives all TOTP/passkey management through `SecurityClient` endpoints, with `SecurityService` holding reactive state and running the browser-side WebAuthn registration ceremony via `startRegistration`.

The SvelteKit logout action only deletes the local cookie (via `deleteAuthCookie` plus an empty value with `expires` at epoch) and never calls the backend, so `AuthService.logout` — the only caller of `POST /api/v1/auth/logout` — is not invoked by the app and the JWT stays valid until it expires.
`authService.getWsTicket()` is used by the accounts list state, which connects to `/api/ws?ticket=...` and reconnects every 5 seconds on close.

Startup configuration rejects a `SECRET_KEY` that is empty or shorter than 32 characters outside `dev`/`test`, and `docker-compose.yml` passes the same value to the frontend service as `JWT_SECRET`, so one secret signs and verifies access tokens, MFA tokens, verification tokens, and WS tickets.

Rate limiting uses slowapi with `user_or_ip_key_func`, which decodes the token with `settings.secret_key` and buckets by `user_id` when possible before falling back to the remote address; signup (5/min), login (10/min), 2FA verify (10/min), resend (3/min), and both passkey authenticate routes (10/min) carry explicit limits.

Signup passwords are validated to 12-128 characters and login passwords to at most 128 characters in the Pydantic request models, and passwords and recovery codes are hashed with `argon2.PasswordHasher` at rest.

Persistent identity state is split across `auth_users`, `auth_verification_tokens`, `auth_totp`, `auth_recovery_codes`, and `auth_passkeys`, with unique constraints on email, verification token, per-user TOTP, and passkey `credential_id`, and cascade deletes on the TOTP/recovery-code/passkey tables.

Auth tests must mock every outbound dependency: the autouse `fake_redis_manager` fixture swaps the shared Redis client with an in-memory fake (with `mock_redis_storage` for assertions), the auth/client fixtures monkeypatch `EmailService.send_verification_email`, and frontend tests must mock every API client and SvelteKit module they touch.

Security-relevant coverage is concentrated in `tests/routers/test_auth.py` (2FA lockout and reset, expired/forged MFA tokens, `mfa_pending` rejection on protected endpoints, passkey challenge expiry and replay, logout denylist), `tests/services/test_auth_api.py`, `tests/services/test_auth_services.py`, `tests/ws/test_router.py`, `frontend/src/hooks.server.test.ts`, and `frontend/src/routes/auth/login/page.server.test.ts`.

Security events are logged with structured `event` names and user ids: `auth.login_success`, `auth.2fa_verify_success`, `auth.totp_enabled`, `auth.totp_disabled`, `auth.passkey_registered`, `auth.passkey_deleted`, and `auth.passkey_login_success`.

Dev CLI commands bypass the normal identity flow: `src/auth/commands/create_test_token.py` mints an HS256 access token valid for 365 days from `settings.secret_key`, and `src/auth/commands/create_test_user.py` inserts a user whose `is_verified` stays at the `False` default.
